canonical_identity.title: Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, Agriculture, and Legislative Branch Appropriations Act, 2026

plain_language_description: At the House-passage stage, an FY2026 funding bill for military construction, military housing, veterans benefits and health care, and related agencies; the Senate later expanded it and the bill remained in conference rather than becoming law itself.
prior_policy_baseline: FY2025 enacted funding for military construction and family housing was $17.509 billion. Congress had not enacted the FY2026 regular bill, so the House vote advanced one chamber's proposal rather than changing current law.
proposed_action_or_mechanism: The House proposal provided annual military-construction, family-housing, and VA funding; directed $29.768 million above the FY2025 enacted level toward expanded military-family-housing oversight; and attached policy restrictions, including limits on certain VA abortion services and on when VA fiduciary determinations could be reported to the federal gun-background-check system.
directly_affected: Related agencies named in the bill

material_scale.house_milcon_family_housing_proposal: $17.989 billion for FY2026, $480 million above FY2025
material_scale.family_housing_oversight: $29.768 million above the FY2025 enacted level
material_scale.note: The paired baseline and selected priorities belong in the 30-second or verification layers; the isolated $17.989 billion figure is not sufficient top-layer context.

implementation_authority: Department of Defense, Department of Veterans Affairs, and related funded agencies, subject to enacted appropriations.
legislative_history: The House passed its version June 25. The Senate passed an expanded version. The House requested a conference in September. H.R. 3944 itself did not become law; related full-year areas were later enacted in a different package, H.R. 5371.

documented_supporter_argument.argument: The House Appropriations Committee majority argued that the package increased military-construction and family-housing funding, raised VA discretionary funding, and supported veterans' care, benefits, facilities, and oversight.
documented_supporter_argument.uncertainty_and_evidence_limits: This is the committee majority's case for the proposal. House passage did not enact the funding, and later H.R. 5371 cannot substitute for this version.

documented_opponent_argument.argument: The committee minority argued that the proposal still underfunded military construction and quality-of-life needs, shifted too much VA care toward community providers, and included eight contested policy riders, while noting that adopted amendments added toxic-exposure funding and protected crisis-line resources.
documented_opponent_argument.uncertainty_and_evidence_limits: The objections and acknowledged amendments are the committee minority's account; they do not establish Foushee's reason for voting Nay.

important_uncertainties: The House-passed text included floor amendments; top-layer copy avoids unsupported line-item precision.
Later H.R. 5371 funding cannot be substituted for the exact policy content of roll 182.
Roll 180 is a mixed en-bloc amendment and remains a separate control.
